ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is yellowish-brown with dark brown blotches. It features a distinct white snout tip, granular skin, and lacks webbing between its fingers.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes agasthyaensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow iris, which contrasts sharply with the darker, mottled body coloration.
ai.habitat: The Agasthya Bush Frog inhabits the high-altitude evergreen cloud forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Agasthya Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged on leaves during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects among the forest canopy.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes agasthyaensis* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females laying small clutches of eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes agasthyaensis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, occurring at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Agasthya Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like series of short, rhythmic "tink-tink" pulses, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude rainforests.
